item.title: MC Eiht Credits GTA: San Andreas For Bringing His Music To Younger Fans
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: MC Eiht said his Ryder role in GTA: San Andreas brought his music to younger gamers while reflecting on his career.
item.content:encoded:
MC Eiht credited Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas with bringing his music to younger listeners. He said playing Ryder introduced him to people who discovered him through gaming.

In a new interview with The Hip Hop Museum, published November 3, the Compton rapper said the game expanded his audience beyond people already familiar with his records.

“It introduced me to a younger crowd who were into gaming and streaming. So it definitely opened the door and bridged the gap between the newer generation and hearing about MC Eiht and Compton’s Most Wanted,” the legendary rapper said.

“I was able to participate in a few parts of the game, first being on the radio stations and then being able to voice and portray Ryder in the actual game. That just took it to another level, and it opened up the doors on the whole gaming industry. Grand Theft Auto was big,” Eiht said.

He also revisited playing A-Wax in Menace II Society, saying he drew on his own experiences to shape the performance. “I ad-libbed a lot of stuff,” he said.

The conversation covered the East Coast relationships behind his music, too. Eiht recalled connecting with DJ Premier, Guru, Pete Rock and Stretch and Bobbito during promotional trips to New York.

Those connections became part of his recorded work. DJ Premier executive produced Eiht’s 2017 album Which Way Iz West and produced four tracks. Brenk Sinatra produced the rest of the album.

The album brought together Eiht’s Blue Stamp and Premier’s Year Round imprints. Its guests included fellow West Coast rappers WC, B-Real, Xzibit and Kurupt, as well as Bumpy Knuckles. Compton’s Most Wanted also appeared on the record.

His latest album, The Story of My Life, arrived October 22. Apple Music lists 20 songs with a running time of one hour and four minutes, under BlueStamp Group LLC.

item.title: Ayesha Curry Addresses Viral Movie Kiss As Steph Backs Lead Role
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Ayesha Curry responds to the viral reaction around her Roku movie kiss as Steph Curry publicly supports her first lead role.
item.content:encoded:
Ayesha Curry addressed the online reaction to an on-screen kiss after a clip from her new Roku movie spread across social media on its premiere day.

The scene comes from Second Chance Holiday, the holiday romantic comedy that gave Curry her first feature-film lead. She plays Chelsey, a dating expert who keeps getting dumped during the holidays and agrees to pose as a couple with her high school flame, played by Matthew Daddario.

Some viewers treated the scripted kiss like a referendum on Curry’s marriage to Golden State Warriors star Steph Curry.

The reaction ignored both the job and the public support Steph gave the project months before its release. When the movie was announced, he celebrated his wife as “My Leading Lady” in an Instagram Story.

Ayesha also made clear why the genre appealed to her. “There’s something truly magical about holiday rom-coms,” she said when Roku announced the film in July. “They invite you into these charming, cozy worlds where anything feels possible.”

The movie is a bigger acting step for Curry, but it is not her first time on screen. Her credits include the 2024 Netflix film Irish Wish, the television series About Last Night and hosting work on food and competition shows. Second Chance Holiday puts her at the center of a scripted feature rather than in a supporting role or as herself.

The Roku production was directed by Maxwell McGuire from a script by Erin Muroski. The supporting cast includes Jasmine Vega, Arcade Riley, Sergio Di Zio and Melissa De Sousa. Roku released the film Thursday, November 5, alongside another original holiday movie, The Holiday Spark.

The viral argument also landed only a few months after Steph and Ayesha marked 15 years of marriage. The couple married in 2011 and share four children. Their anniversary celebration in July was deliberately low-key, according to People.

Ayesha’s response did not turn the scene into anything more than what it was: part of a fictional romance. Second Chance Holiday is now streaming on The Roku Channel, with the attention around the kiss arriving the same day as her first leading film role.

item.title: Lil Baby Says Learning About Politics Changed His Mind On Voting
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Lil Baby says learning more about politics and community power changed his old belief that voting could not make a difference.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Baby is using his own political turnaround to reach people who still believe voting will not change anything.

In an Election Day conversation with Hot 107.9’s “Posted On The Corner,” the Atlanta rapper acknowledged that he once shared that view.

“Every vote counts and I was one of the people that actually believed that voting don’t do nothing for us,” he said.

The station posted the interview on November 4, one day after Election Day.

Lil Baby explained that growing older and learning more about politics and community power changed his thinking.

He said he hopes speaking openly about that change will encourage more people to take part.

This was not an overnight shift.

While discussing the election with V-103 in 2022, Lil Baby said his own lack of political education had shaped what he once believed.

“I know people don’t understand, cause I never was taught this. It’s like we actually do have more power than we think.”

He also urged listeners to research local races, where decisions can land closer to home, and stressed what organized voters can accomplish together.

The Election Day message also connects with the direction of Lil Baby’s work in Atlanta.

On October 17, he said he wanted his nonprofit giving to shift toward jobs and school systems after years of giveaways.

That work has included a $150,000 scholarship fund, but his latest plan is aimed at creating longer-term support.

His education push was visible in July, when Lil Baby’s Back to School Fest helped more than 4,000 Atlanta students prepare for the new school year.

At the time, he explained why the effort mattered to him: “Giving back to my city is everything. You need the right tools to build your future.”

The comment was about supplies and students, but it also showed the local focus behind his newer political stance.

Lil Baby did not present himself as someone who always trusted the system. He described a change that came from learning how local politics works and recognizing that people have more leverage when they act together.

His latest interview puts that evolution in front of listeners who may still be skeptical.

Lil Baby said he hopes his decision to encourage voting can make a difference among people who once felt the same way he did.

item.title: Will Smith Joins The Crowd At Willow’s Birthday Metal Show
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Will Smith joined the crowd at Willow's Halloween birthday party as Animals As Leaders played a private set for the singer.
item.content:encoded:
Will Smith joined the crowd while Animals As Leaders played at Willow’s birthday celebration, with footage from the private Halloween gathering showing the rapper enjoying his daughter’s choice of live music, according to Louder.

Drummer Marco Cirigliano shared the clip on Instagram. Louder described Smith smiling, jumping and bumping into other guests as the instrumental metal trio performed. The outlet reported that Cirigliano identified the occasion as Willow’s 26th birthday, which fell on October 31.

Willow first became widely known for her 2010 single “Whip My Hair,” but her later work moved through pop-punk, heavier rock and jazz.

Willow had already connected with the band’s guitarist, Tosin Abasi. In August, she posted photos of the pair trying the double-neck guitar and bass associated with Angine de Poitrine, Louder reported.

Her interest in heavy music also ran through the family before her own rock records. Her mother, Jada Pinkett Smith, formed Wicked Wisdom in 2002. Willow later made her own place in the genre with Coping Mechanism, her 2022 album that drew on punk, grunge and metal.

She described that range during a Guitar World interview about the record. “We all love pop-punk, it’s beautiful and amazing,” Willow said. “But let’s not forget the metal, thrash and classic rock.”

The singer also spoke about the women who helped make space for her. In a Vanity Fair interview previously covered by AllHipHop, she described women of color playing rock as part of a “beautiful lineage.”

“We’ve been silenced for a long time, and that’s ending,” she said.

Animals As Leaders released Parrhesia in 2022 and were working on a follow-up. The band is a three-piece instrumental group, with Abasi joined by guitarist Javier Reyes and drummer Matt Garstka.

Her releases this year continued that musical exploration. February’s Petal Rock Black was followed by The Thread in July. The latter reunited Willow with producer Chris Greatti, who had worked with her on Coping Mechanism and 2024’s Empathogen. It was her second album of 2026 and her eighth solo record. Its opening track, “She’s My Religion,” featured acoustic guitar, choral voices and percussion, keeping her exploration of sounds beyond pop-punk in view.

item.title: Nicki Minaj’s 13-Point MAGA Post Is Akin To Gibberish
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Nicki Minaj’s 13-point message suggests continued MAGA alignment, casting doubt on Democratic pivot rumor.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj has handed that rumored Democratic pivot a rather inconvenient receipt: her own words. Damn, I thought the rumor might be true. I don’t think so now.

READ ALSO: Nicki Minaj May Try To Go Democrat According To New Rumors

Yesterday, we discussed Media Take Out’s claim that her team was preparing to soften her Republican association while preserving her support for Donald Trump. Then Nicki posted 13 points that sound considerably more like defiance than departure. If MAGA is a cult, she’s got the sugar for the Kool Aid. The message appeared on Twitter (still not calling it X) overnight, reaffirming her support for The Donald and congratulating winners, especially certain Republicans.

Let’s go through them, because somebody’s anonymous source might need to check their messages.

  1. “Trump is STILL your PRESIDENT.”
    That is an emphatic defense of Trump. There is no apparent distancing here.
  2. “The QUEEN is STILL your OBSESSION.”
    She redirects criticism toward her celebrity status. Apparently, political scrutiny also counts toward the fan club.
  3. “Jesus is STILL LORD.”
    A declaration of faith, which by itself tells us nothing about party affiliation. Somehow, I think this is just a dogwhistle to MAGA.
  4. “Great insight by the VICE PRESIDENT.”
    Praise for the administration’s second in command further weakens the suggestion that her support stops with Trump.By the way, JD placed distance between himself and The Donald. That war on the GAZA Strip is a major issue.
  5. “Knowledge is POWER.”
    Knowledge of what?
  6. “Congratulations to all winners! Especially @RepLuna & @ByronDonalds.”
    This is particularly revealing. She specifically celebrates two Republicans, complicating the rumor greatly.
  7. “Blowing a billion on a losing campaign full of celebrities is STILL hurting them.”
    A campaign spending jab, rooted in a lot of nothing. MAGA completely outspent the Dems.
  8. “The BARBZ are STILL PRETTY!!!”
    Trying to shore the base back.
  9. “I don’t vote, I VETO”
    The supplied transcription ends awkwardly. Either way, a presidential veto is an actual government power. Celebrity influence does not come with one. WTF? Does she have power over Trump with that booty?
  10. “Stay tuned & STAY MAD.”
    That sounds like a promise to continue. Nobody is mad. Everybody is happy.
  11. “Christians are STILL being killed.”
    Stop the CAP and the rhetoric. I am Christian, by the way.
  12. “Maybe now our people will WAKE UP.”
    Who, specifically? And wake up to what? FOH.
  13. “Love you”
    An affectionate exit after a fairly combative presentation.

My read: Nicki likely remains aligned with MAGA. Faith and fan appreciation aside, defending Trump, praising his vice president and celebrating Republican politicians make a persuasive combination. People are crip walking, that thing was so blue.

item.title: Yung Miami Says “Spend Dat” Success Gave Her Anxiety Before Solo Debut
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Yung Miami says “Spend Dat” brought anxiety and pushed her to sharpen her debut album Watch Dis before its release.
item.content:encoded:
Yung Miami finally landed the solo hit artists dream about, and it apparently came with a side effect she did not expect: anxiety.

In a new Billboard interview published Wednesday (November 4), the former City Girls rapper said the success of “Spend Dat” made her go back and “hone in” on her debut solo album, Watch Dis.

The song had raised the bar at the exact moment she was preparing to introduce herself as a full-length solo artist.

“I was excited, but I was like, ‘Damn, this is big.’ I want this album to just be great, which I feel like it was. It really made me go back and hone in. Make sure that the album was top to bottom the way I needed it to be,” Yung Miami.

That is a different kind of pressure. Miami was not trying to recreate the record beat for beat. She was trying to make sure the rest of the album could stand beside the biggest solo song of her career.

“Spend Dat” peaked at No. 17 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 2 on the Hot Rap Songs chart, according to the official album announcement. The single was also certified platinum.

The admission adds another layer to a comeback that Miami has framed as a response to being counted out.

When she announced the album, she said she could have returned with one song and played it safe, but she had enough confidence in the music to release “F You” and “2008” on the same day. Watch Dis arrived October 23 through Uptown Records and later debuted at No. 138 on the Billboard 200.

The rapper also told SPIN that she had learned to stop treating social-media commentary as real life.

“You cannot get caught up in that stuff,” she said, explaining that strangers online no longer get to dictate her mood or next move.

That lesson did not erase the pressure that followed “Spend Dat.” Instead, Miami used it as a reason to return to the album and tighten the work. The hit gave her a victory, but it also gave her a new standard to meet.

item.title: Yella Beezy Jury Sees 2019 Interview As Detective Traces Rap Feud
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Yella Beezy's jury watched his 2019 interview and post-concert videos as a detective traced the public feud prosecutors call motive.
item.content:encoded:
Yella Beezy‘s jury watched his 2019 interview and a series of videos posted after a Frisco concert as prosecutors used Day 8 of his capital-murder trial to trace a years-long rap feud with MO3.

Dallas Police Detective Eric Barnes returned to the witness stand and explained why law enforcement treated the rivalry as a public-safety problem. Jurors saw a flyer for the July 2019 Unruly Citizens festival, where both artists were booked. Barnes said officers added security, arrested MO3 on outstanding warrants before he entered and later collected the online responses.

According to FOX 4’s live courtroom report, prosecutors used Barnes to build a timeline stretching back to 2017. Jurors also watched an August 2019 interview in which Yella Beezy discussed surviving a shooting and said street conflict was “two for two.”

He said he did not start problems but finished them when targeted.

The interview was admitted over defense objections. Prosecutors said the material supplied context and mindset for the tension they allege eventually led to MO3’s November 2020 killing. Yella Beezy, whose legal name is Markies Conway, has pleaded not guilty and denied ordering the attack.

Barnes’s testimony followed a day in which the defense challenged Cedric Bradley, a federal inmate who told jurors that White had confessed to him.

Lawyers pressed Bradley about his criminal exposure and an earlier meeting where he denied knowing anything about the homicide. A financial analyst also reviewed Conway’s 2020 bank activity, including two $40,000 withdrawals. The defense argued those transactions fit the spending of a successful entertainer.

The testimony adds a new layer to a case that has already moved through separate trials. White was convicted of capital murder in September and sentenced to life in prison. Brown is separately charged with capital murder.

Barnes also described phone records and surveillance gathered during the investigation, including evidence that a black coupe waited near MO3’s location before the highway shooting. That 18-hour stakeout was aired during White’s September trial and is not new. Thursday’s development was its presentation to Conway’s jury alongside Conway’s own recorded words.

Prosecutors continued playing videos and walking jurors through the history they say explains the killing.

The defense will get its chance to test Barnes’s conclusions and the links investigators drew between music, public arguments and the physical evidence.

item.title: Megan Thee Stallion Calls Out Instagram Over AI Label
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Megan Thee Stallion challenged Instagram after an AI label appeared on photos from her 2026 CFDA Awards appearance.
item.content:encoded:
Megan Thee Stallion wants Instagram to explain why the platform treated her latest red-carpet photographs like computer-made content.

The Houston rapper called out the AI label attached to images from the 2026 CFDA Awards.

A screenshot shared by fans showed her answering the tag with a short challenge: “AI couldn’t generate this lol @instagram fix this please.”

The pictures came from Monday night’s ceremony at New York’s American Museum of Natural History.

Megan wore a custom Kim Shui gown with lacing, cutouts and crystal details. Stylist Isiah Ahmad completed the look with Lorraine Schwartz jewelry and Jimmy Choo pumps.

That matters because the label was not attached to some anonymous image floating around the internet.

It appeared on professional event photography from one of fashion’s most visible nights, where Megan joined Travis Scott, PinkPantheress, Keke Palmer, Lupita Nyong’o and other entertainers.

Instagram’s system has been creating confusion for months.

Testing reported by The Verge found original photographs receiving AI labels while fully generated images sometimes escaped them.

Small edits, background-removal tools and metadata added by editing software have all been blamed for false or misleading flags.

Meta previously said its labels rely on industry-standard signals inserted by other companies. The company also adjusted its wording after photographers complained that a “Made with AI” tag could make a lightly retouched picture look completely artificial.

The problem goes beyond a technical mistake.

Megan’s image, body and public presentation are a major part of her business.

An AI label on authentic event photos can suggest that the person, clothes or setting never existed, even when the picture came from a documented red carpet.

The timing also puts Megan inside a wider fight over trust online. Instagram wants users to know when an image was generated, but a warning loses value if people cannot tell whether it reflects the whole picture, one editing tool or a false positive.

Megan did not turn the moment into a long explanation.

She made the point in one line and put the responsibility back on Instagram to fix its label.

No public explanation was available by early Thursday for why those photographs received the designation.

item.title: Cardi B’s Grow-Good Becomes Top-10 Revolve Brand
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Cardi B's Grow-Good Beauty became a top-10 Revolve brand as repeat purchases rose and lower prices changed the retailer's order mix.
item.content:encoded:
Cardi B‘s Grow-Good Beauty has become one of Revolve’s 10 biggest-selling brands, giving the retailer a new customer pipeline less than a year after launch.

Grow-Good’s third-quarter net sales nearly doubled from the previous quarter, Revolve co-founder and co-CEO Michael Mente said during the company’s November 3 earnings call. Revolve did not disclose the brand’s revenue or its share of total sales.

“Repeat purchases among existing customers have increased meaningfully over the past three months,” Mente said, according to Glossy. He also said the line was already contributing to Revolve’s bottom line.

That matters because Grow-Good is doing more than adding shampoo, conditioner, serum and a hair mask to Revolve’s inventory. Co-CEO Mike Karanikolas said its shoppers have a different profile from the company’s usual fashion customers, although Revolve is “still in the early stages” of understanding their behavior.

Revolve added 202,000 active customers during the quarter, its largest sequential increase. The total reached 3.24 million for the 12 months ending September 30, an 18 percent rise from a year earlier. Karanikolas said Grow-Good played a “meaningful role” in that growth but did not break out how many shoppers it brought in.

The lower-priced beauty products also changed the shape of Revolve’s business. Average order value fell 5 percent to $292. The company said the decline was primarily tied to initial Grow-Good sales at price points well below its fashion assortment. Without the line, the metric would have been roughly flat.

Revolve’s quarterly results showed net sales up 20 percent to $356 million and total orders up 19 percent. Gross profit rose 19 percent to $191.8 million, while adjusted EBITDA fell 7 percent to $23.5 million. The company also said its return rate dropped by more than two percentage points as beauty and international orders became a larger part of the mix.

Cardi and Revolve formally launched Grow-Good in April after a March presale. In October, the brand expanded into independent beauty supply shops in New York, Atlanta, Chicago, Houston and Los Angeles, then staged a day of custom hair treatments at a New York salon.

The third-quarter numbers provide the first clear look at what that rollout is doing for the parent company: attracting more shoppers, producing repeat business and adding profit, even as its lower prices pull down Revolve’s average ticket.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Nicki Minaj’s Own Lawyers Can’t Get Papers Into Her Hands After Three Visits
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: Nicki Minaj's lawyers reported three failed home visits as they tried to hand her papers seeking to leave a $275,149.62 lawsuit.
item.content:encoded:
Nicki Minaj‘s own lawyers sent a process server to her last known home three times without getting their withdrawal papers into her hands, according to a new court filing in her $275,149.62 Jingle Ball dispute.

The visits ended with nobody coming downstairs, word that the rapper was away and another report that she was unavailable.

Her attorneys now want the court to let them leave the case despite the failed attempts at in-person delivery.

Attorney Bruce W. Bieber laid out the efforts in an affirmation filed in New York County Supreme Court.

His firm, Kurzman Eisenberg Corbin & Lever, represents Nicki, legally identified as Onika Tanya Maraj-Petty, and Pink Friday Productions LLC against 24/7 Productions (USA) Inc.

The papers concerned her lawyers’ request to withdraw from that existing lawsuit.

Bieber said the firm hired Nicoletti & Harris to arrange hand delivery after an October 27 order required several forms of service.

The first visit came October 29. According to Bieber’s account of an email from the process-serving company, the concierge had been told someone would come down to accept the papers.

That did not happen. Bieber wrote that “somebody would come downstairs (for purposes of accepting the papers), but nobody came down.”

The server returned October 30 and was told Nicki was not home, although her husband was there. Bieber said the update also reported “that Minaj and her husband have a tendency of not answering their phones.”

A third visit on November 2 ended with word that Nicki was unavailable. No further information was provided, according to the filing.

Her lawyers nevertheless argued that she knew about their effort to leave. Bieber said he emailed the papers October 28 and the firm sent them by certified mail and FedEx October 29.

“KECL has done everything within its power to effectuate in-hand service upon [Nicki Minaj],” he wrote.

Bieber also asserted that Nicki and her company had received several copies and knew about the withdrawal request.

The failed visits followed the firm’s October 23 request to withdraw. Bieber previously cited disagreements over legal strategy and a breakdown in communication.

The underlying lawsuit concerned production work for Nicki’s December 2023 Jingle Ball appearances and New York promotion for Pink Friday 2. 24/7 sought $275,149.62, plus interest and court costs.

The dispute also included a $103,730 Langham New York hotel bill, with a suite priced at $9,500 a night for seven nights.

Nicki’s team contested the demand. In July, her lawyers said the hospitality spending had been approved and Pink Friday Productions had paid the bills. They also challenged the attempt to hold her personally responsible for company debts.

AllHipHop previously reported that Judge Leslie A. Stroth paused proceedings and set a December 1 hearing at 10 A.M. on the firm’s withdrawal request. Answering papers were due November 12, with replies due November 23.

In the new filing, Bieber again asked for permission to withdraw and time for Nicki and Pink Friday Productions to hire replacement counsel.
